incident_description:
I purchased a Kenmore Elite, high efficiency washer with the matching dryer 10 months ago at Sears. Each item was priced at $917.99, so this was no small purchase!  Everything went fine until two days ago. I was washing linens (2 king sheets and a bed liner, no comforter), when I heard an earth shattering BOOM in the garage where my units are hooked up. I raced to see if my house exploded and found the washer rotated 1/4 turn from the wall, the entire top of the washer (the part with the lid AND control panel) was on the ground, and the drum has collapsed inside the unit!! I was scared to death!! I had to unplug the unit to get it to turn off. Thankfully, it JUST MISSED crashing into my hot water heater. 

I called the warranty number that is listed in the manual, and a repair technician is scheduled to come out in four days to look at the unit. REPAIR?? Are you kidding?? I am so traumatized by this incident, I don't know if I trust ANY "so-called" high efficiency washer or dryer units, especially of the Kenmore variety. The representative that took the info said she has NEVER heard of anything like that happening. I have done some research online, and apparently a powerful spin cycle can cause a washer to EXPLODE!! I feel very strongly that this product needs to be looked at and considered for possible recall.
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and emotional distress but no physical injury.

It was the dehumidifier runnning and blowing hot air. I tried to shut it off using the controls on the dehumidifier, but it would not shut off. I had to unplug it from the receptacle. It would have kept running and possible caught fire. I have contacted Frigidaire and was simply told it was not under warranty. That is NOT the issue. It is a FIRE hazard!

incident_description: On November 27yh, 2021 I purchased a Soleil Digital Ceramic Heater Model #PTC-915W (date code 0521) from Walmart in Cheboygan, Michigan 49721.  The heater was purchased for supplemental heat in my seasonal cabin.  The heater was used two times, once in late November 2021 and during the evening of January15th, 2021.  The heater was operated on the low setting throughout the night.  At approximately 4am on Sunday January 16th I awoke from sleeping and was a little chilled.  At  this point I changed the heater setting  to High and went back to bed.  I woke up at 7am to the smell of burning plastic and discovered that the heater had stopped working.  I examined the end of the plug which incorporates a GFI and discovered that one of the prongs was melted and that the plastic receptacle was melted and burned on the hot leg (small slot).  The 15amp breaker for this circuit in the load center was tripped.  This heater was brand new and not modified in any way.  I examined the receptacle for correct wiring, making sure there wasn't a loose Hot, Neutral or ground wire.  All wires were wrapped around the attaching screws and all screws were tight.  I replaced the burnt receptacle and cover.  I reset the 15amp breaker and plugged a different non-ceramic heater into the plug.  The prongs on the non-ceramic heater never got hot and the heater performed correctly.
justification: The heater malfunctioned, causing melting and burning of the plug and receptacle, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I purchased an iron on Amazon and it arrived on 5/31/24. Today, 6/1/24 I took it out to use it. I filled it with water below the max fill line, plugged it in, and used it to iron two shirts. It dripped water all over my hardwood floor, it soaked my ironing board, and it sputtered steaming water all over my shirts. Most of the water leaked onto the floor, and I think it was for the most part room temperature, but I did feel some splatters (small droplets of water) from the impact onto the floor, and they felt hot to me (I was barefoot at the time). The iron is also very lightweight, even with water in it. This, coupled with the fact that it does not stand well on the ironing board because its cord is awkwardly placed, means that it feels likely to tip over. Because of the awkwardly placed cord, the only way to sit the iron upright is to place it right on the edge of the ironing board, with the cord draped over the end. This makes it even more likely to fall. If you read some of the negative reviews for this product on Amazon, you will see that at least one person has been burned from trying to catch the iron as it was falling. Their review is titled "Dangerous" and frankly I agree with them. I don't trust this product not to burn me with scalding water and I'm sure it would have eventually fallen off my ironing board had I continued using it, potentially burning my legs or feet.

incident_description: Eccotemp i12-LP tankless hot water heater.  This unit has a product design defect that allows cold air in through the included venting chimney causing the unit to freeze up even when installed within a temperature controlled room.  The cold air enters the chimney vent and sinks down into the heat exchanger causing it to freeze as there is nothing to prevent the air from entering.  This causes the unit to burst, potentially spraying hot water while also flooding the room in which it is installed.  This, in turn, creates other hazards such as potential electrocution and electrical fire.  Manufacturer does not mention in literature that units should not be installed where subject to freezing.  Retailers continue to sell this unit in states where freezing temperatures are common.  Manufacturer's fix is to "winterize" the unit shutting off water to it and draining any time temperatures drop below freezing even though the unit is required to be installed indoors and the structure is heated.  This, in effect, makes the units useless in Wisconsin 8 out of 12 months of the year.  The manufacturer refused warranty on the project, refused to provide a re-engineered product, and offered the solution to fix it using [REDACTED]!.  These units should be recalled and not allowed to be sold for permanent installation in any state that is subject to freezing temperatures.
justification: The design defect can lead to unit bursting, flooding, and potential electrocution or fire, posing significant injury risks.

incident_description:
Purchased and installed Ideal brand Garage Door with EZ-Set torsion spring.  Garage Door System was installed the summer of 2024. 
a few days ago, the EZ-Set torsion spring winding mechanism failed, resulting in torsion spring becoming detached  heavy garage door to fall  and the garage door overcame the weight of the belt drive opener and dropped. The cause of the failure failed (broken) plastic tabs in the tensioner that are responsible with turning and maintaining torsional force on the spring. These tabs are fragile and should be made stronger (perhaps out of metal) to withstand the extreme force (during all climates including cold temps as we get here in Minnesota). The failure occurred while the door was being raised, so if a person or pet were to be under the door at that time - serious injury (or worse) could have occurred. After I experienced this failure, I found another person on youtube with the same failure - so this is NOT an isolated incident. I did reach out to Ideal door company and they are asking all the warranty related questions - so I simply informed them I was sharing this with you and not pursuing warranty .  The reason I am reporting this is my concern for safety and that hey need to improve the design - perhaps recall?
justification: The incident involved a garage door falling due to a failed torsion spring mechanism, posing a risk of serious injury or death if someone had been underneath. The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) due to the reported similar failure elsewhere, indicating it is not an isolated incident.

incident_description:
ProClean DRYER LINT REMOVAL KIT (Dundas-Jafine) - This 3 component system provides helpful brush/vacuum attachment tools to remove excess lint from dryer trap and vent duct line. However, the recommended procedure, troubleshooting info and manufacturer contact info is incomplete and poses a SAFETY hazard. While initially removing much lint and believing we would restore drying efficiency, our dryer failed to exhaust air to the outside when starting a new load. Hence, after following the limited instructions, it left us with a dryer that did not work and a DRYER OVERHEAT/FIRE RISK HAZARD.

The laundry room became warm/moist, the dryer external surface become very hot, there was no air exiting the vent from the outside. We turned the dryer off and suspected that the lint trap brush may have jammed something inside the dryer to block the internal exhaust. However, and after contacting the kit manufacturer for guidance, we discovered that we actually created a COMPLETE BLOCKAGE in the >10 ft duct line (running underneath the floor) by using the 10 ft. spiral duct brush. We were able to clear that out by aiming a leaf blower from the OUTSIDE into the vent entering the house. We blew out COMPRESSED LINT that filled a 3 gal trash can and had a major mess. NOTE: We used the gas blower from the outside, NOT the inside to avoid sparking the airborne lint in the laundry room (explosion hazard!).

When initially using the long spiral brush in the duct line, my wife and I were able to "pull out" much lint USING IT FROM BOTH SIDES of the duct. It was too short to "snake" all the way through. What we were actually doing in this process was also jamming/compressing the lint in the middle to create the blockage without knowing it (cannot see nor access the middle). So rather than restoring dryer efficiency, the kit process created a VENT BLOCKAGE and DRYER OVERHEAT/FIRE RISK. We were fortunate to observe the overheating/failure to vent, but know many consumers start a load and leave the house or go to bed. Should the dryer over-heat sensor fail, this poses a significant fire hazard.

The manufacturer's Product Development rep was actually very helpful in resolving this issue for our particular experience. Prior to his call, we felt we were going to have to repair or replace our 10 yr old [REDACTED] dryer (which was running OK prior to using the kit, just a little slower to dry). HOWEVER, it was not obvious how to contact the manufacturer for help, and the instructions were sparse. They should call out "post cleaning CHECKS" to confirm the dryer air is venting properly before using again plus trouble-shooting guidelines. There was no manufacturer contact info (e.g., name, phone, etc.) on the instructions, just a name/web address on the carton (which I suspect many would discard since it's hard to fit everything back into the box after 1st use). If no internet access, there is no way to contact them.

I am a retired PRODUCT DEVELOPER of laundry products and familiar with DRYER OVERHEAT/FIRE RISKS. I am filing this report to flag the hazard to others using this product PLUS ANY SIMILAR PROCESS they may use in clearing out the dryer duct line.
justification: The incident describes a significant fire hazard due to a blocked dryer vent, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
We purchased a generator a few years ago.  It was very expensive and between the unit and installation we paid about $12,000.00.  For the past few years it has been serviced by the same business that worked with LOEWS store to install the unit.  We have not had an emergency since we purchased the unit.  We made our purchase to be ready for power outages.  However, on March 2, 2018 during a power outage we experienced system failure on its very first test run.   Shortly after our generator turned on we noticed our lights would flicker and remained flickering for the next few hours our generator was running.  My husband and I was then alerted by our carbon monoxide detectors in our home of high levels of carbon monoxide rapidly rising.  We immediately called the fire department who confirmed high levels of carbon monoxide in our home with the highest reading upstairs where our bedrooms were.  After a thorough search they found the problem could be coming from our outside stand by generator.  They advised us to turn it off.  We were evacuated from our home and instructed to ventilate the home.  They also instructed us to call the gas company and have them check and make sure there were no gas leaks present.  We called our gas company and  our generator service technicians the following morning. The gas company met with us at our home later in the afternoon to run their check.   After turning on our generator during their check for gas leaks the gas technician also confirmed smelling fumes from our generator.  Later explaining to us that there is a difference between propane fumes and exhaust fumes.  He found no gas leak.  The generator technicians came the following day to perform their check.  In our absence he got our generator up and running, later explaining that there was condensation in the unit and that was the cause for the carbon monoxide.  We are still working on getting a solid work order from them for the work performed because we are questioning the findings.  

We are concerned and have questions about our unit.  Is this a manufacture defective unit?  Why didnt our unit shut off?  Should our unit be equipped with a shut off when its malfunctioning?  Is it safe?  Why did the servicing contractor did not handle this as a warranty issue?  Our unit is up to date on routine services and still under warranty.  We even invested on a three hundred dollar warming kit suggested by them as a preventive measure.  Yet on its first test run our generator failed to run safely and properly.  Can someone please contact us regarding our issues?  Our unit is still under warranty and we are trying to get our generator running safely and the way it was intended to run.  We were very lucky to have carbon monoxide detectors in our home, grateful to be well and happy to have the opportunity to address this issue and bring safety awareness to other that this can happen.
justification: The incident involved a generator malfunction leading to high carbon monoxide levels, requiring evacuation but no reported injuries.

incident_description:
The unsafe product is a ""Stanley 5000 Watt Generator with 6000 Surge/Peak Watts" portable generator.  The product was/is sold by SEARS.  The manufacturer of the generator is GXI Outdoor Power LLC.  The product uses the American brand name "Stanley" but is actually made in China by third-parties. 

This product caused a sudden and spontaneous gasoline leak which lead to a fire and decedent's death from 3rd degree thermal burns/injuries. Decedent's wife sustained first and second degree burns and also the emotional trauma of seeing her husband burnt alive, among other things. 

The accident took place on 10/27/14 at approximately 11:30 PM in [REDACTED].  The generator was in decedent's garage and NOT IN USE on the night of the incident. 

When retiring to their bedroom at night, decedent & wife smelled an odor and traced it back to the garage on the ground level.  In the garage, decedent and wife witnessed gasoline leaking from the generator.  Wife tried to obtain rags in the room next door and, upon exiting the garage to the room, the pilot light of the boiler next door ignited the gasoline vapors. 

The New City Police Department, Fire Inspector and Fire Department determined the cause of the fire as being the leaking generator. Thereafter, in Nov. 2015, experts for the estate, SEARS & GXI conducted multiple days of joint inspections, including physical inspection, microscopic testing and chemical testing, among other things.  The joint inspection found a defective, fractured bolt in the carburetor.  The Estate's experts determined the leak was caused by a sudden fracturing of the brass bolt in the fuel reservoir bowl, in the upper portion of the carburetor.  The fracturing of the bolt had caused the fuel reservoir bowl to fall, thereby causing the sudden and immediate leaking of all the generator's gasoline contents.  The experts found that the bolt was made of low quality yellow brass alloy which is prone to corrosion, cracking and dezincification.  The experts also found the bolt had intersecting perpendicular bored holes which also caused the fracturing of the bolt.  All of the above, among other things, constitute dangerous defects in the product.  The experts also found inadequate or non-existent warnings, among other things. 

This report is being submitted as three years have passed and SEARS/GXI have still not reported the incident.  The product is still being sold in the USA, via SEARS, Home Depot, Loews and Kmart.  There is a high likelihood that other American consumers will be injured.
justification: The incident resulted in a death and injuries, and the product is still being sold with a high likelihood of similar incidents.

The incident was unwitnessed and it was unknown what caused the jack to fall.  It was possibly raining at the time of the incident. incident_description:
I purchased and had installed Thermoblaster 32000 BTU Blue flame dual Fuel (Gas) heater in my garage this past weekend and found a issue with the unit that I believe is potentially extremely dangerous! This unit has 2 pilots one that is for natural gas and one for liquid propane. When the unit is started in the proper sequence for Natural Gas both pilots light and should stay on. The problem is when or if the Natural gas pilot goes off for what ever reason the LP gas pilot can stay and does stay lit. This allows the thermocouple to stay latched and in turn allows the main gas valve to open and for the gas to flow out. The problem is the LP pilot flame is smaller and located below the burner outlets as normally LP gas is heavier than air but because the unit is hooked up to natural gas which is lighter than air the gas rises quickly and does not ignite. In my case when the garage reached temperature the unit shut down and the natural gas pilot is going out constantly but the LP pilot stays lit. As stated this keeps the gas valve open and then the whole garage filled with gas to the point where we could smell it outside. I was very lucky that I went out to check on it when I did and that the gas did not build down to the point where the LP pilot could have ignited the gas. If it had I am sure it would have leveled my garage.I did speak to a couple of representatives at Thermoblaster at including the president and they recommended that the LP pilot be capped to prevent this scenario from happening and they even have procedure for doing this. I think this procedure would work but my concern is what if someone does not catch this issue in time. Someone or many could die using this product!
I was able to duplicate this issue a few times and have removed the heater and returned it to Lowes. I think it is also very important to mention that there are a couple of other reviews on the Lowes web site that indicate others have had the same or similar issues with this heater. They should be forced to remove the heater from the market until this safety defect is resolved. rous.
justification: The incident describes a potentially life-threatening gas leak scenario that could lead to an explosion, with multiple reports of similar issues.

incident_description: While investigating why my garage unit heater (natural gas) was not turning on I discovered a tripped breaker.  The Venmar Heat recovery/ Ventilation unit was plugged into the same circuit as the heater.  through process of elimination I found the Venmar to be the cause of the breaker tripping.  I then removed the front cover of the Venmar AVS Duo 1.9 as in performing the annual cleaning, and found the motor to be ~150 degrees F.  I verified that the fan was free to turn (though somewhat stiff) and tried to run it while observing.  The motor appeared to get power, move a few degrees, and lock up.  I isolated the power, removed the motor and lubed the bearings with a couple of drops of oil and was able to free up the shaft to spin freely.  I reassembled and tried powering it up again without the fan cages on the shafts and it immediately bumped, froze up, and heated up.  I did not let it go long enough to trip the breaker.  the motor is apparently not as thermally protected as it should be, and though I haven't disassembled it yet, it may not be designed to be used in a vertical installation.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning motor that overheated and tripped a breaker, but no injury or damage occurred.

I contacted the company on the first unit and they shipped me a replacement at no cost. However a manufacturing defect may exist that has not been brought to the attention of their customers.  Both units were purchased from COSTCO and had a date stamp of "2015 Nov 03" (well short of the 10 year life - that consumers depend on and pay a premium for).  Failure of the product is  a safety issue and requires further investigation and notification to the buying public.  I have contacted First Alert and am waiting for further instruction on what to do with this item. I do not want to return it to COSTCO for a refund since this appears to be an inherent defect that requires further investigation rather than a simple replacement.
justification: The incident involves premature failure of safety devices, posing a potential safety risk, but no injury or death has been reported.

A case number [REDACTED] was opened by GE and later disregarded as an out of warranty product despite having a fire risk.

The fire risk occured when after only 5 years the basket bearing failed.  This resulted in the basket tumbler unit to rock back and forth.   The rubber gasket between the washer basket tumbler and access door heats up from friction during the spin cycle and begins to smoke thus presenting a fire risk.   If the consumer is not home to monitor wash cycles the fire could spread without consumer knowledge while they are away from the home or sleeping.

The estimated cost to repair the washer was $1300 and provided by a GE appliance repair service (Chambers Services, Inc. 1102 1/2 MacArthur Ave., Bloomington, IL 61704 PH [REDACTED] GE was only willing to provide a minimal discount on another GE unit and was not concerned about fire risks.

The washer will be scrapped on 8/17/2012 and replaced by a non-GE made appliance.
justification: The incident describes a fire risk due to mechanical failure, which could lead to property damage or injury if unmonitored.

I installed the system and it functioned fine until October 29th, 2017 when i routinely tested the smoke detector in my basement and it did not make any sound and did not trigger an alarm. Please feel free to reach out to me with any questions or if you need my help to pursue this matter.

https://simplisafe.com/smoke-detector

This is the washing machine where I was my twins clothes, fabric toys, bedding, etc.! They are 7 months old and chew on everything! And my son wakes every night with a stuffed up nose.. Could this mold/mildew be the cause of his breathing problems? Im completely sickened by this. Ive always done any regular maintenance of the machine that is recommended. I never use too much detergent and I rarely if ever use fabric softener... Im mad that I let this happen without knowing but really how could I have known it was like that? incident_description:
The submitter states that the dryer has a defective gas valve. The submitter is filing the report on behalf of his mother.

The submitter indicated that there have been many instances when his mother smelled a gas odor in the home. The submitter believes that the gas valve is getting stuck partially open after being used. The submitter indicated that this occurs randomly and does not occur after every cycle.

The submitter noticed burn marks inside the dryer and on clothes put inside the dryer. The submitter believes the dryer poses a fire hazard.

The submitter contacted Sears about his safety concerns and he was advised that his dryer is not recalled. However, the consumer believes the dryer should be included in recall # 12-251 because it has the same fire hazard as stated below:

"The gas valve in the recalled dryers can fail to shut off properly, continuing to heat the dryer and its contents after the drying cycle is complete. High temperatures inside and on the exterior surface of the dryers can scorch the drum, as well as burn or damage the dryer contents, posing a risk of burn, fire and smoke inhalation."

The submitter indicated that the coil was replaced a few months ago by a third party repair company. The submitter stated that the coil was an original Kenmore part.

The submitter would like the firm to replace the gas valve free of charge but they refused.

The submitter states that a Sears technician examined the dryer today and confirmed that the gas valve is defective.
justification: The defective gas valve poses a fire hazard and has caused burn marks, indicating potential for injury or fire, though no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that she began having headaches she never had shortly after her flooring was installed, and her allergies have worsened.

She visited an allergist and was diagnosed with unexplained idiopathic anaphylaxis. The consumer indicates that she also had ocular migraines on 08/17/2014, to which she was referred to a neurologist. The neurologist ordered an MRI scan on 04/2015, which confirmed a pituitary tumor. After blood-work, it was determined that is was of non-hormonal origins. The consumer indicates that because the tumor is new and she works at a cancer facility, it is being kept under surveillance. In 04/2016, she is scheduled to have another MRI to confirm if the tumor is growing or not; if so, the consumer will be scheduled for surgery.

The consumer has been using an inhaler for the past year, prescribed by her allergist, as she began wheezing - something that never happened before. The consumer states that prior to the installation of the flooring, she never had headaches nor ocular migraines either and so is uncertain if the flooring may be the cause. 

The consumer indicates that the laminate flooring was installed throughout her basement.

The consumer was diagnosed with idiopathic anaphylaxis.  Her condition escalated for a period of time after floors were installed but has subsided at this time.  She doesn't spend much time in the basement.

The [REDACTED] inhaler was used more frequent last year but that has subsided too.  She does not keep the fireplace too warm in the basement.  She has it cooler in case there is release of formaldehyde.

The consumer called Lumber liquidators main office on March 1st 2016 & spoke with [REDACTED] @0915, she stated "we will not send another air quality testing kit & there is nothing we will do because your initial air quality kit came back normal".
justification: The consumer experienced health issues (headaches, allergies, anaphylaxis, and a tumor) potentially linked to the flooring installation, but no direct causation was confirmed.

Her throat burns and she wakes up coughing because the bathroom is right next to her bedroom. It gets better when she is out of the house.  I am not sleeping at my house now to avoid the fumes.

The glue was purchased by the person who installed the flooring.  [REDACTED]

The consumer did not seek medical attention but may see doctor later.

incident_description: My two year old son was taking a bath and the Kohler glass shower door spontaneously exploded on him, causing injury.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to a child due to the spontaneous explosion of a glass shower door.

incident_description:
Between March and April, the consumer noticed that his wife was coughing. The consumer was also having issues with his feet. They were feeling weird and swelling. 

Around the first of April the consumer noticed a rubber or burning smell in the home. On May 9, the consumer was outside of the home and there was a smell of gas. The consumer called the gas company who came out immediately. The problem was with the heat exchange in the furnace. The consumer contacted the furnace company, who also came out on May 11 and condemned the furnace.

The consumer checked on line and saw that there was a class action suit in 2007 in reference to the secondary heat exchange but he was never notified. 

The consumer check online and found out that the issues that he and his wife were having were symptoms of being exposed to polycarbonates in the furnace.

No medical attention was required.
justification: The incident involved exposure to harmful substances from a faulty furnace, causing symptoms but no medical attention was required.

incident_description: The product is a Shark Stick Vacuum Corded version Model Number: HZ2002 12 - UL#: E491422 - S/N: Z06K1206A7A8 Purchased from Bed Bath and Beyond on 12/18/2020 in Rancho Cucamonga CA. After approximately 11 -12 uses, on 6/27/2021 the motor began to heat up to the point of a hazard, based on an inability to continually touch the area of the exhaust fins area over the motor. After allowing the unit to cool for 30-40 minutes I tried again to operate the unit however the excessive overheating occurred again. This was attempted a third time, producing the same results.  I then called Customer Service to address the warranty and the unsafe and dangerous circumstances since online customer reviews revealed that this hazard is being reported consistently by purchasers of this model. The most recent occurrence reviews are 1 week ago, and 4 weeks prior to that (found on the Bed, Bath and Beyond webpage). An even earlier report stated that the plastic housing melted. During my call to Customer Service, they required that I perform the operation again, after opening the dust and floor attachments, which produced the same results of overheating as before. I then contacted one of the Corporate VP's Mr. [REDACTED] at 1327 Hrs on 6/28/2021 to request to speak with someone who can look into the hazardous situation. Mr. [REDACTED] stated that he would determine who I should report this to, and have that person reach out to me for assistance. At this writing (1359 Hrs on 6/28/2021) I continue to wait to receive contact from a corporate representative.
justification: The vacuum overheats to a hazardous level, with reports of melting plastic, but no injury is mentioned. Online reviews indicate this is a consistent issue.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that he has multiple chemical sensitivity. Approximately five years ago, the consumer received three air handlers from the company he worked at and has been using them along with air handler filters from the same company. The consumer noticed that he has been getting sick more often than usual for the past couple of years but he was unsure of the cause.

~03/18/2019 - The consumer contacted the Manufacturer of his air handler filters explaining that they were emitting a chemical-like smell that were making him nauseas, fatigued, irritable, exhausted, and were giving him headaches; he was informed they would send him them replacement filters.

03/28/2019 - The consumer installed the air filters and woke up extremely sick the next day so he states that he knows they are the cause of his deteriorated health. The consumer removed the air filters from the air handlers and has been feeling much better. 

The consumer contacted the Manufacturer and explained the situation; he asked what the air filters contained and was subsequently e-mailed a safety data sheet however it did not contain any chemicals listed.

The consumer indicates that he plans on keeping his air filters for at least the next thirty days in case an investigation ensues.
justification: The consumer experienced health issues (nausea, fatigue, headaches) linked to the air filters, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as the issue recurred over time but was resolved by removing the filters.

incident_description: Kenmore Electric Clothes dryer, model #26-69822 . Start switch was pressed, sparks flew out of console and thick black smoke came out of console. Unit was 6 years old.
justification: The incident involved sparks and smoke but no reported injury.

incident_description:
In October I received FEMA relief funding for the purpose of restoring my electrical utilities due to the loss of equipment and utility related hurricane Helene

I made the purchase off Amazon for 4x2 (8 total) 300w (2400w total) solar panels with the influence of the "Amazon's Top Choice" badge next to the listing. 

After receiving the 8 panels I reported 2 of them as being messed up possibly from shipping. I was given a refund for half the transaction. 

I install the panels, install the new equipment and begin monitoring solar production. The PwM charge controller I was using claimed 44v and 80a output based on my 4p2s configuration. This means I am getting 22.2v and 20a per panel in the 2 strings combining them in series to make the above number. 

I had consistent failures with my solar system due to the battery bank being nearly dead and shutting off by nearly 2am. This continues for months, me spending additional funds and the refund I received on advanced equipment and measurement tools. 

Upon further investigation after replacing every component besides the battery and the panels I discovered an anomaly about the panels themselves. They each had on each polarity junction box a JFET-R voltage regulator which is not a standard blocking diode as other panels have.

Further investigation into this anomaly with more advanced equipment and expert review of the set up determined the JFET-R components are actually hidden Amplifier IC nodes used to amplify the gain of the signal emitted by the solar panels before it can reach measuring equipment so that it reads a false highly inflated number 

A typical solar panel of 300w class is twice the weight of the ones I received, half the amperage output and double the voltage as well as some fair bit larger length or width wise. 

The sticker on the back of the panel had no manufacturer name or information but touted safety and compliance certification badges and the false output of 18.8v and 16a

Further research indicates even a panel of twice the power a typical 300w class photovoltaic cell in the class of 600w output only have a voltage and current reading of 30(some odd)  and 17a with a short circuit of 18 meaning this 300w panel has an isc that outclasses anything in the market at all

The purpose of the purchase was to restore my electrical utilities after hurricane Helene. I am sensitive to heat as a cancer survivor and live year round in a camper. Summer is the time of year I absolutely for medical reasons need to have a method of cooling my environment. Without the full 2400w of solar panels I can not directly power my HVAC system of 18000btu 

I complained to Amazon executive customer relations and received the additional half of my purchase refund at this point it was conveyed in no uncertain terms that I should pursue the manufacturer and I won't be receiving Amazon support for the additional losses related to uncovering the deceptive and fraudulent products. 

In compliance with Amazons statement I research deeply for the manufacturer eco-baeerss according to the seller on the Amazon platform. They can not be found. They are a fabricated manufacturer 

I made the conscious effort to purchase additional equipment equal to inadequate solutions to ensuring I endure the upcoming summer in a albiet extremely suffering but somewhat neutral health condition 

This event has left me to abandon my recovery plan for full restoration of my electrical utilities.  

If I had continued to believe the deception that there is no misrepresentation of the output of the solar array then by the time full peak summer arrived it could have lead to a death of my pet, heat stroke or death in me or my wife. 

That said I am out the allocated relief funding and still do not have adequate utilities even though the purchase of 2400w of panels would indeed have been enough.

UPDATED ON 5/15/2025: [I also was able to find the original manufacturer of the panels who admit the seller and manufacturer on the Amazon site are indeed ficticious as well as acknowledgement of the brand of panel does in fact belong to them

i would be more than happy just to recieve the 2400w i paid for or equivalent with a warranty and at least 50% of the extraordinary purchases made in trying to troubleshoot the falsely labeled panels i did overpay for ]
justification: The incident involved financial loss and potential health risks due to fraudulent solar panels, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: September 5th, 2019 my son was in the bathtub and suffered two lacerated tendons and ligament in his right hand due to a shattered Delta brand shower door.  He was in the tub when one of the two rollers fell off the track above.  One corner of the shower door was resting on the side of the tub. When touched the shower door to raise it back up, it shattered completely.  Instead of small, pebble-sized glass shards, many pieces did not break and fell in hockey puck sized shards, one of which severely cut his right hand.  A visit to the emergency room was required, followed by surgical repair, and weeks of physical therapy.  A follow up procedure is likely in order for him to regain complete mobility in his hand.
justification: The incident resulted in severe lacerations requiring emergency care, surgery, and physical therapy, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: My husband was showering in our new shower and the shower exploded, hitting my husband in the face, hands, midsection, feet and in his eye causing lacerations. The door was hung by professional contractors.
justification: The shower explosion caused lacerations to multiple parts of the body, including the eye, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
A  Pegasus glass vessel sink sold purchased from Home Depot spontaneously exploded  @ 1:30 aAM on May 16th while no one was present in the bathroom, sending glass into our bedroom room where it cut my face in 2 areas, as well as scratched our floor and countertop and left imbedded shards throughout the bathroom and hall area.
Item is Model # SF-02Internet # 100017900Store SKU # 325244Store SO SKU # 375232.
I have seen online that other people have purchased this same sink under the Pegasus and Hembley Creek names and that have also spontaneously shattered. This required extensive clean up and could have killed someone who was in the bathroom. Tiny shards were embedded in the walls. Pieces were in our shower, toilet, bidet and even hit the ceiling. I have contacted home depot to initiate a claim.
justification: The incident caused injury (cuts) and could have been fatal if someone was present, with similar incidents reported online.

incident_description:
The consumer indicates that he was checking the vent of his home heating system and as soon as he propped the vent open, a prong revealed and lacerated his left thumb. The consumer states that it took his thumb approximately one week to heal itself after he placed a bandage on it.

The consumer states that prior to the date of the incident, the unit was used approximately everyday during the Fall, Winter and Spring months.

The consumer is unsure if he will have the unit for the next thirty days. The consumer believes there is a structural flaw in the design of the product as even though he was careful, he was still injured since there were no warning labels.
justification: The consumer sustained a laceration that healed within a week, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident occurred during routine use, suggesting a possible likelihood (3) of recurrence given the reported design flaw.
